layer_meaning.apple_states: Only what Apple's current text (2026-10-30 privacy pages; iOS 27 user guide) explicitly states; stated_as as in the iOS 26 record.
layer_meaning.reasonable_reader: Claude's judgement of what an ordinary reader would expect.

apple.locator: Excluded apps aren’t available to Siri, Search, or suggestions.

unsure.reason: Apple names no data type or action. No touchpoint matches 'an app or its data' for siri_requests or search: app_donated_data is not proven used by those features in current text, and third_party_app_context is tied to Use with Siri, not Excluded Apps.

unsure.item: s27.excluded_apps: taking actions in an app

apple.locator: from taking actions in an app

unsure.reason: An effect on Siri acting in the app, not on a kind of data; no touchpoint exists for it.

unsure.item: s27.excluded_apps: data held by specific apps

apple.locator: or from using data from an app to make suggestions across other apps

unsure.reason: Excluding an app such as Mail or Messages might cover email or messages touchpoints, but Apple does not say which data each app counts as; not recorded.

apple.locator: choose to have highlighted objects automatically sent to third parties to provide results

unsure.reason: Describes what turning the setting on allows; Apple does not state what happens when it is off. Siri AI only (applies_to_this_phone false).

apple.locator: If you do not want Siri Suggestions when sharing, searching, or listening, you can disable Siri Suggestions

unsure.reason: Purpose sentence about suggestions appearing; names no data type or action. It points to the Suggestions screen, which holds four switches; none is named, and no switch for 'searching' is listed on the guide's Suggestions screen.

apple.locator: You can delete the transcripts of your Siri and Dictation requests that are stored on your device by going to Settings > Siri

unsure.reason: Apple states deletion of existing on-device transcripts only. The schema needs stops|continues; stops is used with existing_data deleted. Same applies to s27.siri_ai_turn_off and s27.combo.siri_and_dictation_off. Whether new history stops accumulating is not stated.

apple.locator: When you enable Siri, Apple also collects information about your device specifications, Siri settings, and Siri performance metrics

unsure.reason: On-state only; Apple does not state the off effect. Siri settings is not a touchpoint; request_metadata covers device specs and performance only partly. No claim recorded.

apple.locator: including from third-party apps you allow to integrate with Use with Siri, such as

unsure.reason: Apple scopes sending to apps you allow, which describes the on state; no explicit off statement. Not recorded as a claim, matching the strict reading used for location.siri.

unsure.item: location_device sent_to_apple / approximate location in request data

apple.locator: If you have Location Services turned on for Siri, the location of your device at the time you make a request

unsure.reason: On-state only. September removed the stops claim for this reason (C161, C162). Not recorded.

apple.locator: If you do not want Siri Suggestions when sharing, searching, or listening, you can disable Siri Suggestions

unsure.reason: Apple states a purpose (no Siri Suggestions shown), which is an output effect. No touchpoint in touchpoints.json covers suggestions being shown. Same for s27.suggestions.per_app.show_in_app.

unsure.item: display of suggestions in an app

apple.locator: For example, tap Messages, then turn off Show in App to prevent suggestions from appearing in the Messages app.

unsure.reason: Display effect; no fitting touchpoint.

apple.locator: If you do not want web-based content and search results, you can disable

unsure.reason: Purpose concerns content received, not a data touchpoint. Applies to s27.search.show_related_content as well. No touchpoint fits.

apple.locator: When Search Engine Suggestions are enabled, Safari will ask your selected search engine for suggestions based on what you’ve typed.

unsure.reason: Only the enabled state is described; the guide's purpose (not seeing suggested search terms) is a display effect. Off effect on typed text not stated.

unsure.item: safari_bookmarks / safari_history used for Top Hit

apple.locator: If you disable this option, the page will load normally.

unsure.reason: States only a loading change, not that bookmark or history use stops.

apple.locator: To deliver relevant search suggestions and news, Apple may use the IP address of your internet connection to approximate your location

unsure.reason: Follows the off-state sentence and implies approximation continues, but names no switch, and Apple using an IP address fits none of the six actions. Same sentence on the Search page after the global Location Services statement. Not recorded.

apple.locator: If you do not want your Search queries to be stored by Apple and used to improve Search

unsure.reason: The stops claim for Siri searches combines the paragraph's definition (Search requests including those made using Siri) with Apple's opt-in exception. Apple does not say it in one sentence. Review whether to keep.

apple.locator: The data being processed in Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple.

unsure.reason: No touchpoint or action for requests sent to Private Cloud Compute (Apple says not stored or accessible to Apple). Related: requests are not sent to Private Cloud Compute if Siri AI is not enabled or not available (s27.use_siri_classic).

unsure.item: not sent to Private Cloud Compute

apple.locator: your request is not sent to Private Cloud Compute and is processed on-device whenever possible

unsure.reason: Direct statement for the Siri AI not enabled state, but there is no touchpoint/action for Private Cloud Compute.

unsure.item: Siri app conversation history and its iCloud sync

apple.locator: If you enable Siri AI and use iCloud, the history of your interactions with Siri that are saved within the Siri app will also sync

unsure.reason: On-state only; no touchpoint for Siri app conversation history (transcripts_on_device is the Siri & Dictation history). Off effect not stated.

apple.locator: the audio from when you set up Siri to recognize your voice syncs using end-to-end encryption

unsure.reason: Apple does not say whether turning off Siri in iCloud stops this (September N14). No claim.

evidence.locator: if you choose to allow apps to use Speech Recognition for transcription, the audio data to be transcribed may be sent to Apple

unsure.reason: Would be audio x app_speech_recognition x sent_to_apple. Apple states only the allowed state; it does not say that disallowing an app stops the audio being sent. Not recorded as a claim.

evidence.locator: Siri suggests content you might like based on on-device processing of information derived from the apps you use

unsure.reason: Apple states the switch disables this ('You can disable this at any time'), but no touchpoints.json id covers 'information derived from the apps you use' (app_donated_data is 'donated or contributed' information, not the same words).

evidence.locator: recommendations are based on your reading habits in the News app only, not in Safari and other apps

unsure.reason: The 'other apps' / 'apps you use' part has no matching touchpoint; only the Safari part is claimed (as safari_history).

evidence.locator: Siri can suggest events found in Mail, Messages, and Safari

unsure.reason: Events found in Safari may not be Safari browsing history; no claim made for safari_history.

evidence.locator: Siri: Allow Siri to make suggestions across apps based on the way you use Mail.

unsure.reason: No touchpoint for usage of an app. app_donated_data is the nearest id but Apple's wording differs. Same wording on Notes and App Store pages.

evidence.locator: To allow Siri to make suggestions in other apps based on how you use Calendar, turn on Learn from this App.

unsure.reason: Purpose clause states an effect, but no touchpoint for 'how you use Calendar'. September mapped Learn from this App to app_donated_data via a privacy-page sentence that now routes to Excluded Apps instead.

evidence.locator: Siri also suggests adding contact information in other apps based on how you use Contacts.

unsure.reason: With 'To turn off either feature, see Exclude apps from Siri, Search, and suggestions.' this is a purpose_of_instruction, but 'how you use Contacts' and 'your activity in other apps, such as Mail and Calendar' do not match the contacts or email touchpoints exactly. Also the instruction is a pointer to Excluded Apps, not a named switch.

evidence.locator: searches Mail, Messages, Wallet, and Calendar for related information

unsure.reason: Call Context (Apple Intelligence) uses email and messages, but it is none of the five features in touchpoints.json; Apple states only that the cards turn on or off. applies_to_this_phone false.

evidence.locator: if you opted in to Personal Requests on HomePod, phone call status

unsure.reason: Phone call status 'may be shared locally with your nearby Apple devices' only if opted in. Not one of the six actions; nearby_device_status also covers timers, alarms, media and proximity, which this switch does not gate.

evidence.locator: Tap Screen Time, tap Content & Privacy Restrictions, tap Siri, then do any of the following:

unsure.reason: Route conflict: privacy page says Other Features > Siri; guide says Content & Privacy Restrictions > Siri. No data effect either way.

apple_states.claude_note: Apple states only that the phone stops listening for the phrase. Nothing is said about sending, storage or review of audio. Mapping listening to used_on_device is Claude's reading.

reasonable_reader.note: Apple's sentence (and the O105 footer) says the phone stops listening for the phrase. A reader expects the phone no longer to listen to their speech for Siri this way.
